subject.title: RFC: single-writer state materialization via the queue DO (retire git-lease concurrency)

question: Should ClawSweeper adopt the queue Durable Object as the authoritative single writer for state materialization, or continue hardening the current Git-lease publication model?
rationale: The proposal changes the durable write authority, failure model, and migration/rollback contract; current merged work only mitigates contention within the existing model and cannot establish the desired long-term architecture.

options.title: Approve a staged single-writer design
options.body: Authorize a design-and-pilot phase that preserves the lease path as rollback until each lane has proven idempotent append, materialization, recovery, and reconciliation behavior.

options.title: Retain Git publication coordination
options.body: Keep the merged lease and priority model, add the proposed compaction and repository-size guardrails, and defer materializer work.

recommendation.title: Approve a staged single-writer design
recommendation.body: Authorize a design-and-pilot phase that preserves the lease path as rollback until each lane has proven idempotent append, materialization, recovery, and reconciliation behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The RFC and the most recent state-publication recovery and fairness changes indicate the strongest current ownership signal for the architecture decision.
